title: Fast ACS: Low-Latency File-Based Ordered Message Delivery at Scale
problem: Delivering messages with ordering and at-least-once delivery guarantees across clusters to thousands of consumers while maintaining low latency and enabling consumer-controlled pacing.
motivation: Real-time distributed systems require efficient low-latency message delivery infrastructure that scales to global consumer populations.
method: Fast ACS uses two-sided communication (RPC) for inter-cluster messaging and one-sided communication (RMA) for intra-cluster delivery, with file-based storage providing ordering guarantees. The hybrid approach selects the appropriate primitive based on message distance to optimize end-to-end latency while maintaining ordering and delivery guarantees.
key_novelty: Hybrid RPC/RMA communication strategy that optimizes message delivery latency by selecting the appropriate primitive based on inter-cluster versus intra-cluster distance.
contributions: File-based ordered message delivery system combining RPC and RMA primitives
Production deployment at scale across dozens of clusters supporting thousands of consumers per cluster
Demonstrates Tbps-scale intra-cluster message throughput with sub-second p99 latency
Low-overhead infrastructure for global message distribution

metrics.other: p99 latency: sub-second to few seconds; intra-cluster throughput: Tbps scale

primary_theme: Hybrid RPC/RMA communication for ordered message delivery
